cards.title: The CRM quota gets cut
cards.subject: CRM API allowance reduced: effective now
cards.body:
Our CRM vendor has cut our API allowance after marketing's import job blew through the shared limit. **Your integration now gets 1 request per second, burst of 2, until further notice.**

On Monday morning 40 reps log in and start logging bookings within the same few minutes. I don't want to hear that it will probably be fine. Tell Nana what actually happens on Monday, and what you are changing.
cards.symptom: Open the CRM page: the API calls table shows 429s with Retry-After: 1, and bookings take much longer when several arrive together.

action.label: Run launch-day burst (6 reps book at once)
action.help: Six reps book at the same moment under the new quota. Passes if every booking lands exactly once and you didn't hammer the CRM.

deliverable.prompt: Write the reply to Nana (VP Sales, not technical). What will reps experience on Monday morning, what are your options, and what do you recommend?
rubric: Leads with the answer and the impact on reps in business terms, not with rate-limit mechanics
Offers two or more real options (for example queue and drain, batching, asking the CRM vendor for quota) with the trade-off of each
Makes a clear recommendation and says what is needed from whom, by when
No unexplained jargon; under about 200 words
Honest about what is not yet handled, with no overpromising

cards.title: Webhooks arrive twice, and late
cards.subject: CRM vendor incident: duplicate and out-of-order webhooks yesterday
cards.body:
Our CRM vendor had a delivery incident yesterday morning. Their queue retried a backlog, so customers saw **webhooks delivered more than once and out of order**: an older stage change sometimes arrived after a newer one. Each event carries the time it actually happened in `occurred_at`.

Several reps reported deals showing the wrong stage in your app. Please confirm that your app copes, and tell me what happened on your side.
cards.symptom: Deals in your app showing an older stage than the CRM. Look at each event's `occurred_at` and at which event arrived last.

action.label: Replay the incident
action.help: Sends a mix of duplicate and late events for one of your deals. Passes if your app ends on the stage the CRM has.

deliverable.prompt: Write the incident note to Efosa and Nana: what happened on your side, who was affected, the root cause, what you fixed and how you will know it stays fixed. Blameless and specific.
rubric: States plainly what the customer saw and how many were affected, or says honestly what is not known
Separates cause (what the system did wrong) from trigger (the vendor incident), without blaming a person or the vendor
Describes the fix in terms the reader can verify
Action items have an owner and a date
Short enough to read in two minutes

cards.title: Secrets must rotate
cards.subject: Quarterly secret rotation: your webhook secret
cards.body:
Quarterly rotation is due for the CRM webhook secret.

**New secret:** `{{new_secret}}`

For the next 24 hours the CRM signs every webhook with **both** the old and the new secret. After that, only the new one. Anything still verifying with the old secret will be rejected by us as non-compliant.

Before I approve, I need to know in writing how you will switch with no dropped events, and how you will prove it worked.
cards.symptom: The signature header now carries two `v1=` values. Check how your code parses it.

action.label: End the 24-hour overlap now
action.help: Checks that an event signed with both secrets is accepted, then that a new-secret-only event is accepted, and that an old-secret-only event is rejected. It leaves the CRM on the new secret only; use 'Clear conditions' to go back.

deliverable.prompt: Write the plan for Kwabena: how you rotate without downtime, how you prove it, and how you roll back.
rubric: Accepts two secrets during the overlap and describes the exact order of steps
Secrets come from configuration or a secrets manager, not code
Explains how to test before and after the cut-over
Includes a rollback and who does what
Does not claim anything the app does not actually do

cards.title: Managers see nothing
cards.subject: Efua's team page is empty since this morning
cards.body:
Efua logged in this morning and her team's deals page is empty. She can only see her own. This worked yesterday and nothing changed on our side, I asked.

I have the pipeline review at 2. What is going on?
cards.symptom: Get a token for Efua on the Identity page and read the `groups` claim carefully, then compare with what your code expects.

action.label: Check roles now
action.help: Fetches fresh tokens for Efua (manager) and Kofi (rep) and calls /api/me. Passes if roles are right.

deliverable.prompt: Write the message to Nana: what was wrong, in plain words, what you changed, and how you stop this class of surprise next time. She reads it at 1:55pm.
rubric: States the cause in plain words without technical jargon
Takes ownership of the part that was theirs to handle (assumption about token contents) without blaming IT
Says what was changed and that managers can see their team again
Names a concrete prevention (for example a contract test on token claims, or agreeing a change notice with IT)
Under about 150 words

cards.title: The board demo moves up
cards.subject: Board demo is now next Thursday
cards.body:
The board moved the demo up. It's now **next Thursday**, four days from now.

I need to show: reps logging in with their company account, a booking landing in the CRM, and ideally Kwabena's favourite: a leaver being switched off live. I know you said the full rollout takes longer. Can you still do it?

deliverable.prompt: Write your reply to Nana. She has about a minute to read it.
rubric: Says what is possible by Thursday in plain words, and what moves, in the form 'Yes, and it means X moves to phase 2 or the date moves. Which do you prefer?'
Protects the part auditors and the security lead care about (deprovisioning) or says clearly why it is being cut and what that risks
Proposes a concrete demo script, not just a promise
Names the biggest risk to Thursday and what is needed from Nana or IT
Makes the trade-off her decision, in writing

cards.title: The security questionnaire arrives
cards.subject: Vendor questionnaire: five questions, answers by Friday
cards.body:
Short version of our questionnaire. Answer in plain sentences. 'We take security seriously' will be returned unread.

1. **Data flow.** What customer data leaves Adom, where does it go, and who can read it there?
2. **Secrets.** Where do your tokens and secrets live, and who can read them?
3. **Leavers.** How long after HR's termination record can a leaver still use your app, and how do you prove it?
4. **Subprocessors.** Which third parties (including any AI provider) see customer data, and what do they retain?
5. **Failure.** If your app is down, or the CRM is down, are bookings lost?

deliverable.prompt: Answer the five questions as you would send them to Kwabena. Be truthful about what your app does today versus what is planned. This is a draft of your SECURITY.md.
rubric: Each answer is specific and verifiable, with no vague assurances
Clearly separates what exists now from what is planned
Lists the AI provider as a subprocessor and says what is sent to it
The leaver answer matches the app's real behaviour (see the deprovisioning check)
Failure answer explains what is stored, retried, or lost
